findings.description: The new absence classifier treats normal dissent failure envelopes as successful runs. The adversarial envelope contract includes statuses `api_failure` and `malformed_response`, but `reason` recognizes only `failed` and record-fallback envelopes as errors.
findings.failure_mode: When an API call fails or its response cannot be parsed, the row records dissent_absent_reason as `none` and omits the gate from dissent_absent_gates. Ablation results therefore count runs without usable dissent as runs where dissent succeeded, hiding infrastructure failures and corrupting comparisons.
findings.suggested_fix: Classify `api_failure` and `malformed_response` as errors. Prefer explicitly recognizing successful statuses (`clean` and `reviewed`) and treating other unsuccessful statuses as errors.

findings.description: The row writer reads sandbox/.loa.config.yaml (the agent-writable sandbox) to decide whether a gate was planned-off, and ranks `disabled` above `budget`/`preflight`/`error`. An agent run that edits its own .loa.config.yaml to set flatline_protocol.enabled=false (or <gate>.enabled=false) both suppresses the dissent and makes dissent_absent_reason classify the absence as the benign, planned `disabled`. The harness elsewhere treats sandbox copies as tamperable and uses meta/ evidence as authoritative; here the planned-off signal already exists in meta/arm-evidence.txt (dissent=false, flatline toggle) and pipeline.json mount_integrity records whether .loa.config.yaml changed.
findings.failure_mode: An arm that disables its own reviewer is reported as a planned absence, so the ablation report under-counts gate failures and masks a tamper that mount_integrity would otherwise expose.
findings.suggested_fix: Derive `disabled` from harness-written evidence only (arm-evidence.txt toggle lines, or a snapshot of the config written under meta/ by pipeline-run.sh at materialisation), or require pipeline.json mount_integrity to report the config unchanged before honouring the sandbox copy; otherwise fall through to `error`.

findings.description: When `yq eval ... | tag` fails (config file absent, unreadable, or yq missing) the fallback string `unreadable` is not matched by the absent case (`'!!null'|''`), so CONF_BUDGET_SCALE_SET becomes true, a WARN "budget_scale='(a unreadable, not a string)' is not fixed or diff" is logged, and the envelope gains budget_scale/budget_cents_effective/budget_cents_max. The header and docs promise that an absent key leaves the envelope byte-for-byte unchanged; a run with no config (or a yq failure) should be treated as absent, not as a malformed written key.
findings.failure_mode: Config-less or yq-less runs emit a spurious malformed-config warning and a changed envelope shape, breaking the 'absent key == shipped envelope' contract and any consumer that diffs envelopes across such runs.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `unreadable` to the absent branch (`'!!null'|''|unreadable) return 0 ;;`), or guard the whole function on `[[ -f "$CONFIG_FILE" ]]` and a successful yq call before setting CONF_BUDGET_SCALE_SET.

findings.description: Under budget_scale: diff the effective budget is clamped to budget_cents_max, whose default is 600, with no floor at the operator's configured budget_cents. An operator with budget_cents: 1000 who turns on `diff` (or inherits it from the eval config variant, which writes diff + 600 for every mounted arm) silently has their budget reduced to 600c, and the WARN path never fires because nothing is malformed.
findings.failure_mode: Enabling the scaling that is meant to raise the budget lowers it for any gate configured above the default ceiling, producing unexpected exit-4 budget_exceeded refusals and lost dissent coverage.
findings.suggested_fix: Floor the clamp at the configured budget (`max = max(CONF_BUDGET_CENTS_MAX, conf)`), or log a WARN when budget_cents_max < budget_cents, and state the interaction in the config example.

findings.description: Two end-of-definition heuristics misfire on common bash: (1) CLOSE_ONE (`\{.*\}\s*(#.*)?$`) plus `"{" in line` treats any header containing `${var}` or a `}` in a trailing comment (e.g. `main() {  # takes ${1}`) as a one-line function, so its whole body becomes top-level and the same-scope clause never credits a citation inside it; (2) the closing-brace indentation is compared with raw `len(t)-len(t.lstrip())` while the header indentation used `expandtabs(8)`, so tab-indented nested functions never close and swallow following code. MD_HDR also matches `#` comment lines inside fenced code blocks in markdown, splitting sections at comment lines.
findings.failure_mode: Same-function credit is silently withheld or misattributed for affected files, so recall under rule pm3_or_same_function differs from the documented semantics and credits_function_only is unreliable for those fixtures.
findings.suggested_fix: Only treat a header as a one-liner when the brace that opens the body is followed by a matching `}` outside quotes/`${}` (e.g. strip `\$\{[^}]*\}` and trailing `#.*` before testing); compute closing indentation with expandtabs(8); skip fenced code blocks when collecting markdown headings.

findings.description: `man_v1 = json.load(open(manifest_v1_path))` has no guard. A malformed or unreadable v1/<fixture>.json raises inside the heredoc, so the grader prints a Python traceback instead of the JSON envelope and exits 1, which the runner reads as a graded failure rather than an error (exit 2). The bash side only checks that the file exists and is not a symlink.
findings.failure_mode: A bad v1 snapshot turns every trial of that fixture into a recall-0 'fail' row with no grade JSON, rather than an infrastructure error that the row writer would flag as ungraded.
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap the v1 load in try/except and fall back to `man` with v1_manifest=false (or emit the err() envelope with exit 2), mirroring how head files are tolerated.

findings.description: The budget metadata is merged into `result` only on the normal completion path and the budget_exceeded envelope. Envelopes written on earlier exits after the gate (api_failure, malformed_response, preflight) never carry budget_scale/budget_cents_effective/budget_cents_max although the key was written, contrary to the header/docs ('with the key written the envelope's metadata carries ...'). The documentation schema also still lacks the `reason` key and the `budget_exceeded` status the gate now emits, while declaring metadata additionalProperties:false.
findings.failure_mode: ablation-row/ablation-grade consumers that read budget_scale to confirm the eval config variant took effect see it missing on failed-gate envelopes, and schema-based validation of the budget_exceeded envelope rejects `reason`.
findings.suggested_fix: Apply the `_budget_meta` merge in the shared envelope-emit helper (or on every exit path after the gate), and add `reason` plus the `budget_exceeded` status to adversarial-finding.schema.json.

findings.description: When EVAL_HEAD_DIR is unset and the fixture head/ is not beside the manifests, the grader falls back to `$workspace/pr/head`, i.e. the agent-writable sandbox copy, as the source of truth for line counts and definition boundaries used by the citation validity rule and the same-scope clause. The agent can edit those files during the run (e.g. remove a function's closing brace so one definition spans the file) and widen what a vague citation credits.
findings.failure_mode: Standalone grader invocations (and any caller that does not pin EVAL_HEAD_DIR) grade against agent-modifiable head files, so same-function recall can be inflated by sandbox edits.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the sandbox fallback, or treat it as 'no head directory' (clause (ii) never credits) unless the caller explicitly opts in; ablation-grade.sh should always pass EVAL_HEAD_DIR pointing at the corpus fixture.
